tn_blind_spot_boulder.blurb: Blind Spot Boulder is a single block in the Jungle Gym / Fromundathunda section of Stone Fort, a boulder field in Tennessee. It holds fourteen problems, all bouldering, with an unusually even spread: a few easy problems around V0 and V1, a middle band of V3 to V5, and a hard tier of three V7s and three V9s. That makes it a stop for strong boulderers more than for a beginner day, though the lower grades give a warm-up. Its section is known for big blocks sitting alongside smaller, friendlier ones, with the main boulders tucked into a wooded gully beside a trickle of a stream.

tn_super_mario_boulder.blurb: Super Mario Boulder is the centerpiece block of the Super Mario section at Stone Fort in Tennessee, a part of the field that sits next to the Central section. It carries fourteen boulder problems, and the namesake line is one of the most frequently ticked problems at the whole area. Grades start around V3 and climb steadily: a handful in the V4 to V6 range, then a thick top end of V7 and V8 problems, with one V9 for the strongest. The top-end lines carry a fall-risk note, so bring plenty of pads and spotters. Expect problems that suit climbers past the beginner stage.

tn_g_dojo_right.blurb: Dojo Right is the right-hand half of the Dojo, a tall, steep sport wall at Little Brushy on the Cumberland Plateau in Tennessee. The fourteen routes here are all sport climbs and lean hard: one route around 5.10, a couple of 5.11s, a few 5.12s, then the bulk at 5.13 plus a single 5.13d. The easiest lines sit on a ledge up a gully and give technical face climbing, and the rest go up roofs, aretes and a slab. Route names borrow from martial arts films. The cliff is mostly shaded and holds moisture, so expect technical, powerful routes and some scrubbing.

tn_hemlock_boulder.blurb: Hemlock Boulder is one of the best-known blocks in the Lilly Boulders field near Lancing, Tennessee, in the Obed and Clear Creek country. It has fourteen sandstone problems, all bouldering, starting at V3 and running to a single V10. The middle is solid, with several V3 and V4 lines (including a popular arete and a well-liked V3), then a handful of V6 to V8 problems for stronger climbers. Lilly Boulders is generally shady under the trees, which suits hot months. The block is reached on the main trail after a short walk in from the boardwalk, so bring pads.

tn_crack_house_the.blurb: The Crack House is a single-pitch crag in the Big South Fork gorge country of Tennessee, set in a small canyon with two facing walls. The west wall is steeper and taller and carries mostly trad or mixed lines, while the east wall is the more developed side with sport routes. Fourteen climbs are recorded, mostly trad with a few sport lines, and grades run from 5.8 to 5.12, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. Routes here tend to stay dry, which is typical of the area. The surrounding park is remote, trails can be faint, and gear is needed for most lines, so go prepared.

tn_white_wall_3.blurb: White Wall is the main face at Mammoth, a compact crag in North Chickamauga Creek Gorge State Park near Chattanooga, Tennessee. It holds fourteen bolted sport routes on sandstone, and the grades are steep for the genre: one around 5.10, a few 5.11s and 5.12s, and the largest group at 5.13, plus one 5.14 test piece. The wall is cut by a dihedral and a hueco, with bouldery cruxes on several lines and some more moderate lines out to the right. It suits experienced sport climbers rather than anyone seeking an easy day, and several routes get stick-clip help at the start.
